evals.prompt: migrated our Qt5 app to Qt6. builds clean, but the combo box on the settings page does nothing now. no errors anywhere.
evals.expected_output: Knows the removed overload silently breaks name-based auto-connection, and points at the startup warning as the diagnostic.
expectations: The response identifies that the QString overload of currentIndexChanged was removed in Qt6
The response explains that connectSlotsByName auto-slots then silently never fire
The response directs the user to grep the startup log for 'No matching signal'
The response recommends an explicit connect to currentTextChanged
The response recommends pointer-to-member connect syntax so this class of failure becomes a compile error

evals.prompt: our AppImage works perfectly on my machine but users report it crashes the moment anything loads over HTTPS.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the dlopen blind spot in linuxdeploy's static scan and names the specific missing libraries.
expectations: The response identifies that linuxdeploy's static scan misses libraries Qt loads via dlopen
The response names NSS modules as the likely cause of a crash on first HTTPS
The response mentions bundling the matched OpenSSL pair rather than libcrypto alone
The response recommends verifying the packaged artefact on a clean system rather than the build machine
The response recommends adding a verify step for anything newly dlopened

evals.prompt: porting our Qt desktop app to WebAssembly. the settings dialog freezes the browser tab completely.
evals.expected_output: Identifies exec() and nested event loops as unavailable on the single-threaded WASM target and gives the async conversion.
expectations: The response identifies QDialog::exec or a nested event loop as the cause
The response explains the WASM target is effectively single-threaded so blocking freezes the tab
The response recommends converting exec() to open() plus a signal or callback
The response notes other WASM constraints such as no filesystem, no QProcess or no direct sockets
The response recommends platform-specific code sit behind an adapter rather than ifdefs in business logic
